title: Box 3.01 Agents with sufficient evidence and agents with limited evidence of gastric carcinogenicity in humans
copyright: IARC Monographs on the Evaluation of Carcinogenic Risks to Humans [Internet]. Lyon (France): International Agency for Research on Cancer; List of classifications by cancer sites with sufficient or limited evidence in humans, IARC Monographs Volumes 1–137; updated 2019 July 30. Available from: https://monographs.iarc.fr/agents-classified-by-the-iarc/
tablehtml:
Agents with sufficient evidence of gastric carcinogenicity in humans

·    Helicobacter pylori infection

·    Rubber manufacturing industry

·    Tobacco smoking

·    X-radiation and γ-radiation

Agents with limited evidence of gastric carcinogenicity in humans

·    Art glass, glass containers, and pressed ware (manufacture of)

·    Asbestos (all forms)

·    Epstein–Barr virus

·    Lead compounds, inorganic

·    Nitrate or nitrite (ingested) under conditions that result in endogenous nitrosation

·    Opium consumption

·    Pickled vegetables (traditional Asian)

·    Processed meat (consumption of)

·    Salted fish, Chinese style

legend: Intramucosal signet-ring cell carcinoma (pT1a). Small focus of loose signet-ring cells restricted to the mucosa
source:
Imported from 5th edition

van der Post Rachel

legend: Early gastric cancer. Intramucosal carcinoma with structurally abnormal  crowded glands with cytological atypia. The glands in the submucosa are displaced non-neoplastic glands.

diagnosis: Early gastric cancer with poorly cohesive carcinoma
legend: Early gastric cancer with poorly cohesive carcinoma.  Signet ring cells are seen within the mucosa, and includes cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm in the deep layer and cells with vesicular and mucus-rich cytoplasm in the superficial layer. The center of the lesion has sparse carcinoma cells due to secondary change.
Hepatoid adenocarcinoma. The tumour is composed of large polygonal eosinophilic hepatocyte-like neoplastic cells
Adenocarcinoma with enteroblastic differentiation. The malignant glands consist of  columnar neoplastic cells characterized by glycogen-rich clear cytoplasm, reminiscent of fetal gut epithelium

Micropapillay adenocarcinoma. Note small clusters of tumour cells without fibrovascular cores protruding into clear spaces. The tumour cell clusters display characteristic 'inside-out' growth pattern with the luminal aspect of the cells present on the outer surface of the clusters
Tubular adenocarcinoma. The tumour is composed of dilated or slit-like branching tubules of varying diameter invading the stomach wall

Mixed adenocarcinoma. The tumour displays two distinct components: tubular/intestinal carcinoma and poorly cohesive carcinoma (non-signet ring cell type) with signs of lymphovascular and perineuronal invasion
Papillary adenocarcinoma. Note the elongated finger-like processes lined by columnar or cuboidal cells with pleomorphic nuclei, supported by fibrovascular connective tissue cores
Type 0-I, endoscopic features. A slightly reddish protruding lesion with irregular surface, 16 mm in size, located in the lesser curvature of the lower gastric body.
source: Mitsuhiro FUJISHIRO, MD, PhD mtfujish-kkr@umin.ac.jp (for usual communication), mtfujish@gmail.com (for with >3Mb attachment) Manager and Associate Professor Department of Endoscopy and Endoscopic Surgery, Graduate School of Medicine, The University of Tokyo 7-3-1, Hongo, Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo, Japan (zip code: 113-8655)

legend: A Early gastric carcinoma type 0-I, histological appearance (low-power view). The tumour displays features of papillary adenocarcinoma.

Type 0-IIc, endoscopic features. A discoloured, depressed lesion with irregular margins, 18 mm in size, located on the posterior wall of the gastric angle.

legend: C Early gastric carcinoma type 0-IIc, histological appearance (low-power view). The tumour displays features of signet-ring cell carcinoma.
Type 0-IIc, histological appearance (high-power view).
Borrmann type I. A large, polypoid, and fungating tumour with broad base; the surface has a variegated appearance.
Borrmann type II. An ulcer-forming mass with elevated base in relation to the neighbouring mucosa, which appears as a thick wall surrounding the ulcer.
Borrmann type III. A large ulcer with a surrounding zone of infiltration; thick gastric folds fuse each other at the ulcer edge, indicating cancer infiltration.

diagnosis: Gastric adenocarcinoma, Borrmann type IV, an extreme example (linitis plastica)
legend: Whole stomach with prominent gastric folds, which resemble hypertrophic gastric rugae; the waffle-like appearance of the folds indicates loss of extensibility due to scirrhous infiltration of cancer cells; note a small ulcer between large folds on the posterior wall (arrow).

diagnosis: Gastric adenocarcinoma, Borrmann type IV, an extreme example (linitis plastica)
legend: On the cut surface, diffuse white streaks delineate the submucosa, muscularis propria, and subserosal layer; note a shallow ulcer in the centre of the lower slice (arrow; corresponds to the arrow in Fig. <<44361>>).
A Low-power view of gastric carcinoma with lymphoid stroma; note lymphoid follicles in the submucosa adjacent to the carcinoma.
source: Dr Hiroyuki Abe Department of Pathology Graduate School of Medicine, the University of Tokyo

legend: B Note carcinoma cells forming small nests or fused glands, accompanied by abundant lymphocyte infiltration.
source: Dr Hiroyuki Abe Department of Pathology Graduate School of Medicine, the University of Tokyo

legend: C Gastric carcinoma with lymphoid stroma with the nuclei of carcinoma cells staining positive by in situ hybridization targeting EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER). Nuclei of infiltrating lymphocytes are negative.
source: Dr Hiroyuki Abe Department of Pathology Graduate School of Medicine, the University of Tokyo

legend: Hepatoid adenocarcinoma consisting of sheets and cords of polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, closely resembling hepatocellular carcinoma.
source: Prof. Tetsuo Ushiku Department of Pathology Graduate School of Medicine, the University of Tokyo

legend: Invasive micropapillary adenocarcinoma displaying tumour cell clusters with the characteristic inside-out growth pattern, and luminal pole of the cells present on the outer surface of the cluster.
source: Prof. Tetsuo Ushiku Department of Pathology Graduate School of Medicine, the University of Tokyo

legend: Adenocarcinoma with enteroblastic differentiation with the glands lined by columnar neoplastic cells, characterized by glycogen-rich clear cytoplasm, reminiscent of fetal gut epithelium.
source: Prof. Tetsuo Ushiku Department of Pathology Graduate School of Medicine, the University of Tokyo

legend: Tubular adenocarcinoma. The tumour is composed of dilated tubules invading the muscle layer.
The tumour consists of elongated finger-like processes with fibrovascular connective tissue cores, lined by columnar cells.
Malignant glands are seen in extracellular mucinous pools.
Nests of signet-ring cells are present floating in extracellular mucin.
Poorly cohesive carcinoma, signet-ring cell type. The tumour is composed predominantly of signet-ring cells; the neoplastic cells are larger at the superficial part of the mucosa.
Poorly cohesive carcinoma, non–signet-ring cell type. The tumour consists of poorly cohesive cells of non–signet-ring cell type that invade the gastric wall widely, with marked desmoplasia.
B Mixed carcinoma with a poorly cohesive cell component.
Tubular component.
Lymphatic invasion by poorly cohesive cells.
Vascular and perineural invasion by the tubular component.

diagnosis: Gastric adenocarcinoma of fundic gland type
legend: Submucosal invasion is noted on low-power view in the central portion of the tumour.
source: Takashi Yao, MD, Department of Human Pathology, Juntendo University School of Medicine, 2-1-1 Hongo, Bunkyo-Ku, Tokyo, Japan, 113-8421 (e-mail: tyao@juntendo.ac.jp). )

diagnosis: Gastric adenocarcinoma of fundic gland type
legend: At high magnification, the invasive carcinoma consists of neoplastic cells of immature fundic gland type.
source: Source: Takashi Yao, MD, Department of Human Pathology, Juntendo University School of Medicine, 2-1-1 Hongo, Bunkyo-Ku, Tokyo, Japan, 113-8421 (e-mail: tyao@juntendo.ac.jp).

legend: A Type 1. A large polypoid and fungating tumour with broad base; the surface has a variegated appearance.
B Type 2. An ulcer-forming mass with elevated base in relation to the neighbouring mucosa, which appears as a thick wall surrounding the ulcer.
C Type 3. A large ulcer with a surrounding zone of infiltration; thick gastric folds fuse with each other at the ulcer edge, indicating cancer infiltration.

D Type 4. Diffuse gastric wall thickening with prominent gastric folds; the waffle-like appearance of the folds indicates loss of extensibility due to scirrhous infiltration of cancer cells (linitis plastica).
Tubular adenocarcinoma consists of dilated tubules. Necrotic debris is seen within the lumen.
Papillary adenocarcinoma consists of elongated finger-like processes with fibrovascular connective tissue cores, lined by neoplastic columnar cells.

diagnosis: Poorly cohesive carcinoma, signet-ring cell type
legend: Poorly cohesive carcinoma, signet-ring cell type, is composed of neoplastic cells with signet-ring morphology, characterized by an eccentrically placed nucleus and clear to eosinophilic cytoplasm. These cells are smaller in the deeper regions and significantly larger in the superficial part of the lamina propria, showing a layered structure.

diagnosis: Poorly cohesive carcinoma, not otherwise specified
legend: A This example of carcinoma consists of invading, poorly cohesive, non–signet-ring cells eliciting an extensive desmoplastic reaction.
A,B Note solid tumour islands. The differential diagnosis includes neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), hepatoid adenocarcinoma, and squamous cell carcinoma.
In mucinous adenocarcinoma, malignant glandular epithelium lines mucinous pools and is seen floating within these extracellular pools of mucin.
This mucinous adenocarcinoma has signet-ring cells floating in mucinous pools.
In this mixed carcinoma, adenocarcinoma with papillary and tubular structures transitions into a poorly cohesive carcinoma with signet-ring cells.
Lymphoid follicles are seen on low-power view, within and around the tumour in the submucosa.
Histological appearance is reminiscent of lymphoepithelioma (nuclei of carcinoma cells were positive for EBV-encoded small RNA [EBER] by in situ hybridization).

This example of adenocarcinoma is characterized by glands lined by columnar neoplastic cells with glycogen-rich clear cytoplasm, reminiscent of fetal gut epithelium (nuclei of carcinoma cells were positive for SALL4 by immunohistochemistry).
A The tumour consists of neoplastic cells of oxyntic gland type, irregularly anastomosing and invading from the mucosa into the submucosa.
A,B Note solid tumour islands. The differential diagnosis includes neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), hepatoid adenocarcinoma, and squamous cell carcinoma.
B This type of adenocarcinoma consists of neoplastic glands of oxyntic gland type, irregularly anastomosing and invading from the mucosa into the submucosa.
A This example is composed of tubular and poorly cohesive components.
C E-cadherin immunostain underscores the loss of expression in the poorly cohesive component.
A Hepatoid adenocarcinoma consists of sheets of polygonal cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm, resembling hepatocellular carcinoma (tumour cells were positive for AFP by immunohistochemistry).
A Tubular adenocarcinoma with crawling pattern. This is a characteristic anastomosing/fused growth pattern, with distended, abortive, and spiky glands.
The tumour consists of irregularly shaped tubules lined by columnar neoplastic cells.
B A very well differentiated adenocarcinoma with low-grade nuclear atypia, mimicking foveolar hyperplasia.
Elongated, finger-like projections with fibrovascular cores are observed within the lumen, lined by neoplastic columnar cells.
Signet-ring cells are noted, confined to the superficial mucosa, transitioning to other discohesive cell patterns lacking mucin.
B PASD-resistant intracytoplasmic eosinophilic globules can be seen in some cases.

diagnosis: Poorly cohesive carcinoma, not otherwise specified
legend: B Note invasion of the muscularis propria by discohesive cells showing marked cellular atypia.

diagnosis: Macroscopic classification of early gastric cancer (<strong>Type 0</strong>)
legend:
Macroscopic classification of early gastric cancer (Type 0).
Type 0-I (protruded). Type 0-IIa (elevated). Type 0-IIb(flat). Type 0-IIc (depressed). Type III(excavated). Superficial tumours with two or more components should have all components recorded in order of the surface area occupied, for example, “Type 0-IIc+ III”
